applies_why: The text weighs the challenger's chain against the defender's chain in a single collision (D6 vs C1), which is exactly the chain-against-chain situation this rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: the phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words': reading one, the judge's 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' is the retired stating-verse test applied against the challenger's chain; reading two, it is only a footing observation that the Joseph link lacks support anywhere in the chain, which weighing by footing permits — I chose reading one because the judge had already affirmed the chain 'is footed', so the defect doing the work is the absence of an own-words naming, not absent footing
why: Having found both chains footed, the judge still marks the challenger's chain down because no verse in it names Joseph as begetter, letting the retired stating-verse consideration rather than footing alone drive the outcome, which K-C forbids for either side.
